title: Filolial Master
paragraphs: “Ugh… Father. That was pretty harsh.”
I said that on the way back from the audience.
“Still, Sakura-chan and the others seemed to be having a great time, didn’t they?”
“True… I don’t remember ever seeing Princess Melty look like that before. Yuki and the others seemed to be having fun, too.”

After the meeting, we returned to the reception room for a moment. By the way, Éclair is here with us, too. What’s this? Are you my enemy as well? If that’s the case, I’m going to make sure you work hard from now on.
“You’re just like a Filolial Master, Second Princess.”
“That’s my title!”
Why on earth does my Finacée have such an enviable title?!
“I’m a Filolial Master, too!”
“A self-proclaimed Filolial Master…”
“I, too, feel that Lord Kitamura’s unwavering resolve is reassuring to witness. Now then…”
Having said that, Éclair bowed to the representatives of Siltvelt before responding with a salute. It feels like she brushed it off rather casually.
“Once again, my name is Eclair Seaetto, dispatched from Melromarc to serve as the Hero’s bodyguard.”

“Given her track record of assisting the Shield Hero on his journey from Melromarc to Siltvelt, her lineage as a representative of friendship, and her personal qualities, there could hardly be a more suitable candidate.”
The representative of the Shusaku race nodded, looking convinced. So there are no objections, then.
“Regarding the battle the other day, she also served as a liaison with the Queen of Melromarc. I’m sure anyone in Siltvelt would acknowledge her.”
The elder of the Genmu race doesn’t seem inclined to raise any objections either. Well, judging by the patterns of previous loops, Éclair should be trustworthy.
“As the representative of Siltvelt, I grant permission for Éclair Seaetto to serve as the Shield Hero’s bodyguard.”
And so, it seems Éclair has officially been added to Father’s bodyguard detail.
“Nice to meet you, Ms. Éclair.”
“Hmm. It seems you’ve gained some new companions, Lord Iwatani and the others, since I last saw you.”
Éclair turns her face toward Panda and Zou.

“Yeah. How should I put it… There’s Ms. Larsazusa, who distinguished herself in the last war, and Ms. Elmero-Puhant, who captured Takt’s sister. Because they each achieved great feats, they’ve been appointed as my Guardian Knights and will be serving as my bodyguards.”
“I see. As you’ve probably heard many times before, I’m Eclair Seaetto. We’ll be working together from now on. I’m counting on you.”
Saying that, Éclair extends his hand for a handshake. Panda shakes hands with Éclair.
“Alrighty then. I’m Larsazusa. Let’s skip the formalities, shall we? Don’t make a big deal out of rank and all that, okay?”
Panda replied to Éclair in a slightly rude tone.
“Rasa, that’s rude. I’m sorry. This guy’s a mercenary through and through; he was promoted to the rank of knight because of his outstanding performance.”
“I see… In Siltvelt, there’s a tendency to find beauty in the wild. I, too, have no intention of getting hung up on trivial matters. Now then… Did you say your name was Elmero-Puhant?”
“Yes. I’m a newcomer who was just appointed today, but I look forward to working with you.”

By the way, Zou always walks around the castle in a crouched position. His head hits the ceiling, you see. What’s more, depending on the location, he can’t even pass through some hallways or doorways. It seems his massive frame causes him all sorts of trouble. Melromarc Castle wasn’t built with the kind of large-framed people found in Siltvelt in mind.
“Puhant… Ah, so you’re from that renowned family in Siltvelt—one whose name is renowned for its strength, separate from the Four Representative Clans?”
“…Yes.”
Zou nods, turning his face away slightly. Éclair tilted her head ever so slightly as she shook hands with Zou.
“You call me a former mercenary, but you, of all people, used to be a good-for-nothing so-called knight, didn’t you? And how long are you going to keep pretending to be a borrowed cat?”
“Lasa!”

It seems Panda and Zou are the kind of pair who bicker precisely because they know each other so well. I feel like Father and Finacée from my first world were like this. They must get along incredibly well.
“No, please don’t worry about it. Lars-chan really does have a sharp tongue, hehehehe…”

“It’s no problem. I’m sure you’ve heard about the history between Lord Iwatani, the Shield Hero, and me, but please don’t let it bother you too much. You’ve all been appointed because you each have your own roles, haven’t you?”
“You bet. I’m not really in the mood to get too aggressive, though.”
“Yes. I’m well aware. It’s an honor just to be entrusted with this duty.”
It seems he’s speaking as if he’s fully aware of everyone’s individual motives.

“Well, I imagine Lord Iwatani and the others can already defend themselves quite well on their own, but since we’re all knights… I’d be happy if you could let me know later just how skilled you all are.”
“Sure thing. My shoulders have been a bit stiff lately, so this might actually be good.”
“It’s easier to join forces once we know how strong our fellow knights are.”
Zou’s tone is starting to soften a bit. Does that mean he finds it easier to talk to someone like Éclair?
“I suppose I’ll have to show off my ‘Bamboo Grove’ moniker, won’t I?”
“Not quite as impressive as the Queen of Earthquakes, though.”
I can tell that Mera Mera, Panda, and Zou are all burning with fighting spirit. “Bamboo Grove” and “Queen of the Earthquake”? Hmm… I’ve heard that phrase somewhere before. Where was it again?
“They’re both pretty cool, aren’t they?”
“The Love Hunter! Motoyasu Kitamura can’t let himself be outdone either.”
“Well, in Motoyasu-kun’s case, it’s just a self-proclaimed title…”
“Hmm, I’m truly looking forward to this. So, Lord Iwatani, what is your original purpose for coming to Melromarc?”
Whoops, I almost forgot. The original purpose is the Eternal Filo-chan Project.
“Ah… If I tell Ms. Eclair, won’t it get back to the Queen of Melromarc?”

“Lord Iwatani, I, too, hold a position involving classified information. I have no intention of doing anything that would put us at a disadvantage regarding issues in Siltvelt, with whom we’re building friendly relations.”

“Well, that’s good to hear… To put it simply, there are various things I need to do in Melromarc to establish governance in Shieldfreeden and deal with the remnants of Takt. Based on information I gathered using Motoyasu-kun’s knowledge, that is.”
“I see…”
Perhaps because I’d been talking about loops and such earlier, Éclair believed me without a second thought. It went smoothly—that’s good.
“Also… well, we’ve got our own scandal here—one serious enough that we can’t be blamed for Aultcray’s escape. I’d like to settle things on that front as well.”
“Given the current situation, Melromarc can’t really press the issue, so that’s not a problem. So, what exactly happened?”
“Takt’s Dragon Core Stone was stolen. That’s why we need to take various measures on the Melromarc side.”

Oh... This is a story that won't make sense unless you understand how the Dragon Emperor works. Well, Éclair must have heard a little about it along the way, but she probably doesn’t know the details.
“Hmm… This has some similarities to the Aultcray incident. It’s highly likely the same culprit is behind both.”
“Yeah. Well, since we could’ve asked the Queen about this part already, it’s fine if we talk to her about it later.”
“Is that okay?”

“Yeah. Motoyasu trusts me, and after actually talking to him, that’s what I concluded. So… regarding this Dragon Core Stone—I’ve learned that, depending on how it’s used, it could summon a monstrous beast, so I want to take precautions… and I’d like you to make the call.”

“Understood. As for the details, just let me know once Lord Iwatani… or even Siltvelt makes a decision. After all, I was dispatched here to protect Lord Iwatani and the others from Aultcray’s rampage.”
Hmm. Éclair is a serious person, so I don’t think there will be any problems, generally speaking.

“So… according to Motoyasu-kun’s information, it seems a plague is spreading due to the carcass of a dragon that Ren defeated in the mountains east of Melromarc. Can you confirm this? It’s something we’d like to handle.”
“Hm? Was there such a report? Well then, I’ll go check it out.”
“Naofumi, Sakura, I want to play with Mel-chan.”
“I wanna play!”

Sakura and Kou must be getting bored—they’ve started begging Father. No, you mustn’t! If you interact with your Finacée any further, your Heart gauge will go up. You absolutely must avoid reaching MAX Hearts.
“Well, we’ve got some time before we move on… Alright, go ahead.”
“Then let me take you to Second Princess Melty. Feel free to play to your heart’s content in the castle gardens.”
“Okay!”
“Yay!”

T-This… the way things are going, I can’t very well say no. I guess I have no choice. Well, since my Finacée won’t harm Sakura-chan and the others, I’ll let it slide just this once. Just this once, mind you!
“Yuki-chan, you should go too.”
“Yes, ma’am!”
Zou is watching Sakura-chan and the others as they act like that.
“…Elmero-san must be feeling a bit cramped… Yeah, could you keep an eye on Sakura-chan and the others?”
“But…”
“It’ll be fine since Lars-chan and Motoyasu-kun are there. Actually, I’d like you to make sure Sakura-chan and the others don’t wander off on their own.”
Father sensed the situation and asked Zou. Zou then bowed deeply before replying.
“Thank you very much. Well then…”
“Father! May I come along too?”
“Since Motoyasu is the only one who knows the exact location, I’d be in trouble if you weren’t here.”
“Come on now!”

And just like that, Éclair led Sakura and the others, along with Zou, out of the room. The representative of the Shusaku clan and the elder of the Genmu clan also left, saying they had business to discuss with the nobles of Melromarc. It seems they’re taking this opportunity to discuss matters with a group of people who share similar aspirations to Éclair’s.

Before long, cheerful giggles could be heard coming from the castle gardens. Looking out the window… it seems Zou is letting Sakura-chan and the others—including his Finacée—ride on his head, or lifting his trunk to show them even higher up.
“That’s not really his style, is it…”
Panda replied, muttering to himself.
“Does Elmero-san like kids?”
“Well, I don’t know… but I do get the feeling he likes giving people a ride. If anything, I think he was doing it to have his subordinates carry out precise attacks.”

Being an elephant, he’s a bit rough around the edges, I suppose. However… if I may say so, his way of babysitting doesn’t seem quite as skillful as Father’s or my Older Sister’s. It’s different from being good at taking care of people or enjoying it… the phrase “likes children” seems to fit him perfectly.
“It does suit him, actually. He gives off a vibe where you feel you can trust him with them.”

Father has a soft spot for people who are good with children. In that sense, I suppose the people from Siltvelt made the right choice. I’ll have to be careful. Just as I was watching this scene from the window, Éclair returned.
“Lord Iwatani, Lord Kitamura, excuse me.”
“Welcome back, Ms. Eclair. How did it go?”

“Hmm… Based on Mr. Iwatani’s testimony, I checked with the castle’s intelligence services and the Adventurers’ Guild, but apparently, no such incident has occurred in the eastern region of Melromarc.”
“Huh?”
“To begin with, there are no reports in Melromarc of a dragon being slain by the Sword Hero.”

Father is looking right at me. That said, at this time of year, Ren would have been hunting dragons in the eastern part of Melromarc as a stepping stone, and their corpses should have rotted by now. Still, if they say it didn’t happen, then I suppose it didn’t. So let me try to recall what Ren was like around the time the first wave ended. It was quite a while ago, so my memory is a bit fuzzy…

“If I recall correctly, Ren was complaining that after Melromarc had weathered the first wave, he was told something like, ‘We’ll be in trouble if the Trash don’t step up their game.’ It was because of that unpleasant incident that he said he was going to flee to Zeltoble.”
I’m pretty sure that’s what he said.

“That’s because Lord Kitamura had just demonstrated his formidable power by forcibly breaking through the border fortress. There’s testimony that he made that remark under the influence of that incident.”

“So does that mean—because of Ryo’s distrust of the country, he only leveled up a little and didn’t defeat the dragon he was supposed to take down first, or that the dragon he was supposed to defeat after going to Zeltoble hasn’t been vanquished yet?”
Good heavens… that means that dragon is still alive in this world. That pathetic dragon who claims to be the weakest of them all, mind you.
“Does that mean this was a wasted trip?”

Well, Ren only has one body, so there are limits to what he can do. As a result, he may have given up on the dragon in order to escape Melromarc. No… given Ren’s personality, what if he simply didn’t want to contribute to Melromarc, a country he dislikes? That might be the case.

“No… assuming that child is still inside Motoyasu’s spear, if we raise a dragon near me or Motoyasu, the soul of the child who was originally meant to be that dragon might be torn out. It’s dangerous, but I think we should first test whether that child can do it—that way, we can avoid causing any unnecessary tragedy.”

“You’re being strangely considerate, Father. Isn’t it fine to not worry about a Rival’s life or death? I’m sure his parents and Assistants would just accept it as a mysterious death and move on, following the law of the jungle.”
“No… honestly, what’s the point of causing them any more grief? If it’s possible, there’s no harm in giving it a try, right?”
“There’s the time lost from having to go meet that dragon-like creature.” But when I said that, Father looked genuinely exasperated, so I decided to keep quiet.
